A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiTAR research and contain 21 complete pages, including Appendices A–C. Text, equations, tables and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original DiTAR benchmark results, subjective ratings, scaling experiments, ablations and inference measurements in Tables 1–7 and Figures 2–6.

after.justification: v4 retains the original DiTAR experimental results, including benchmark evaluations, subjective ratings, scaling analyses, ablations and inference measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same aggregation encoder, causal language model, LocDiT, historical context, LM guidance, training objectives and temperature-sampling procedure. Algorithm 1 is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain the same training coverage and evaluations on LibriSpeech subsets A/B, Seed-EN and Seed-ZH. The text-only voice-diversity scenario is also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within Tables 1–3, including the NaturalSpeech, E2TTS/F5TTS, MaskGCT and CosyVoice comparisons. The efficiency study retains the same NAR comparator.

E3.justification: Dataset subsets, metrics, model configurations, training budgets and inference settings are retained. Both describe ten English raters, 500 syntheses under each temperature setting, and the same A100 efficiency protocol.

E4.justification: The component-scaling, patch-size, historical-context, LM-guidance, temperature and efficiency analyses are unchanged. Removing the duplicated scaling passage does not remove an analysis or its evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version adds seed information, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 and Figures 2–6 retain the same results and trends. For example, Table 3 reports DiTAR WER of 1.685% on Seed-EN and 1.023% on Seed-ZH in both versions.

T1.justification: The autoregressive factorization, diffusion and temperature definitions, and Appendix A.3–A.4 derivations are mathematically unchanged. No assumptions, proofs or formal properties are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning patch-based autoregressive diffusion, temperature sampling, scalability, speech quality and computational efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations of component scaling, historical context as outpainting, the temperature diversity–stability tradeoff and inference efficiency are retained. No substantive limitations or applicability qualifications are added or removed.

D1.justification: Section 3.5 and Appendix A retain the same implementation, preprocessing, hardware, optimizer, training and model-configuration details. The project-page and technical resource links are unchanged.

R1.justification: The 62 references, Section 2 discussion and Appendix C comparison with other autoregressive diffusion frameworks are unchanged. Research positioning and novelty relationships are retained.

P1.justification: v3 duplicates Scaling Behaviors in Sections 4.2 and 4.3. v4 keeps one copy as Section 4.2 and places Experimental results and Comparison with Additional Models under Sections 4.1.2–4.1.3. Subsequent headings, cross-references and the date are updated; most prose is unchanged.

P2.justification: The structural correction redistributes existing displays: Table 5 moves from page 11 to 10, Figure 4 from page 12 to 11, and Figure 6 from page 13 to 12. All eight tables and nine figures are retained without substantive display-content changes.

improvement.justification: v4 removes the redundant Scaling Behaviors section and restores the benchmark results to the appropriate Section 4.1 hierarchy. This makes the experimental narrative easier to follow while preserving all scientific content and appendix material, yielding a limited editorial improvement.
